newsitem.title: UK: Fat women have trouble getting jobs - Finnish study.
newsitem.headline: Fat women have trouble getting jobs - Finnish study.

text.p: Fat women have a harder time finding and keeping a job than slim women, Finnish researchers reported on Thursday.

They said their study of 6,500 Finnish women aged between 25 and 65 showed obese women were more likely to be unemployed. They also had a lower household income and were more likely to have a low income if they did work.
"Obesity was associated with unemployment and economic problems in females," Sirpa Sarlio Lahteenkorva of Helsinki University told the Eighth European Congress on Obesity in Dublin.
Lahteenkorva said she accounted for age, education, region where people lived and long-term illness.

But she said she did not know whether obese women were being discriminated against purely for appearance reasons, whether something else might link their trouble getting work and their obesity, or which came first - the obesity or the inability to get good jobs.
"It's really impossible to say, especially when it is a question of discrimination," she said in a telephone interview from Dublin.
"Nobody tells you don't get a job because you are obese -- usually you just don't get it. But other studies have shown that obese people are evaluated as having poor character."
Lahteenkorva found just the opposite for men.
"I didn't find any problems with unemployment with men. It was the thin men that were having most of the problems. They were more likely to have low income and problems finding a partner," she said.

She said people could get caught in a cycle of unemployment and weight problems. "Personally I think it may be both -- that obesity affects socio-economic status and socio-econonomic status affects obesity," she said.
"If you are overweight, being unemployed may increase your weight. When you don't have anything to do you tend to eat."
Lahteenkorva said her findings probably applied across industrial societies, "especially when you are talking about affluent Western countries because we value good looks," she said.

"People tend to value things that are not easy to achieve. In the old days in developing countries where obesity is rare and food supplies are limited, obesity is usually associated with high status."
